# app-tokens

Command: `boundary app-tokens`

The `app-tokens` command lets you manage the app token resource in Boundary. You can use app tokens for machine-to-machine authentication.

## Examples

The following example creates an app token by passing in a scope and permissions. You can pass permissions directly
as a JSON array or as a path to a JSON file using the file:// prefix, for example, `file://perms.json`.

```shell-session
$ boundary app-tokens create \
  -scope-id $SCOPE_ID \
  -name "Example App Token" \
  -description "An example app token in the global scope." \
  -time-to-live 30d \
  -permissions '[{"grants":["id=*;type=target;actions=list,read"],"grant_scopes":["this"]}]'
```

**Example output:**

```plaintext
App Token information:
  Approximate Last Access Time:   Thu, 01 Oct 2026 18:04:09 PDT
  Created By User ID:             u_1234567890
```

## Usage

<CodeBlockConfig hideClipboard>

```shell-session
Usage: boundary app-tokens [sub command] [options] [args]

  # ...

Subcommands:
    create          Create an app token
    list            List app tokens
    read            Read an app token
    revoke          Revoke an app token
    delete          Delete an app token
```

</CodeBlockConfig>
